finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only check is a substring match for "example.io" anywhere in the URL, so any host passes. The default http.Get client also follows redirects, so the check can be bypassed further. The response body is returned to the requester.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo") (query or POST body, unauthenticated; route registered at main.go:43)
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) (default client, redirects followed) with the body copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: /logo route registered with no auth middleware
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") — substring check, not a hostname check
http.Get(raw) — DefaultClient, follows up to 10 redirects, no IP/private-range/scheme restriction
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — internal response returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: main.go:32 substring check: bypassed by putting "example.io" in the path or query, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:6379/?example.io or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io. No hostname parse, no allowlist, no CheckRedirect (so a trusted-looking URL can 302 to an internal host), no blocking of loopback, link-local, or RFC1918 addresses. Only Go's built-in http/https scheme support limits the schemes. Error from http.Get is ignored (resp may be nil, then the defer panics), which is a crash issue, not part of this SSRF finding.

verdict.guard_found: Only main.go:32 strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), a substring check that does not close the finding. No hostname parse, scheme or IP restriction, or CheckRedirect on the default client at main.go:36. The stricter /cdn handler (main.go:20, 24) is a different route and does not guard /logo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, the substring check at main.go:32 is bypassable with a query like http://127.0.0.1:6379/?example.io, main.go:36 calls http.Get with the default client that follows redirects, and main.go:38 copies the response body back to the requester on the unauthenticated route at main.go:43.
